items.prompt: Which way does heat flow between two objects?
items.answer: From the hotter to the cooler

steps: Heat flows from hotter to cooler.

items.answer: When two objects reach the same temperature

items.prompt: A hot spoon in cool water: which cools and which warms?
items.answer: The spoon cools and the water warms

steps: Heat flows from spoon to water.

items.prompt: Why does a hot drink cool to room temperature?
items.answer: Heat flows from the drink to the cooler room

steps: Heat flows to the cooler surroundings.

items.prompt: Does heat flow on its own from cold to hot?

steps: Heat flows from hot to cold, not the reverse.

items.prompt: When does heat stop flowing between two objects?
items.answer: When they reach the same temperature

steps: At equal temperature, net heat flow stops.

items.prompt: A cold soda on a warm table will do what?

steps: Heat flows into the cold soda.

items.prompt: What kind of energy flows between objects at different temperatures?
At thermal equilibrium, are the temperatures equal or different?
Does the hotter object warm up or cool down as heat flows?

steps: The hotter object cools as it loses heat.

items.prompt: Explain what happens when a hot and a cold object touch.
items.answer: Heat flows from hot to cold until both reach the same temperature

items.prompt: Explain why a cold drink warms up in a warm room.
items.answer: Heat flows from the warm room into the cold drink until they match

steps: Heat flows into the colder drink.

items.prompt: Why does heat flow stop at thermal equilibrium?
items.answer: Because the objects are at the same temperature, so there is no net flow

steps: Equal temperatures stop net heat flow.

items.prompt: Give evidence that heat flows from hot to cold.
items.answer: A hot drink cools and a cold drink warms toward room temperature

steps: These show heat flowing hot to cold.

items.prompt: Predict the result of mixing hot and cold water.
items.answer: They reach a single in-between temperature (thermal equilibrium)

steps: Mixing reaches equilibrium at an in-between temperature.
